body:
# Independent audit: comonotone barycentric face laws

Source: `candidate a60ee1969152d817`.

Full Sections 1–4 PASS. No mathematical repair is needed. This audit
uses the upper-tail submeasure comparison directly rather than a
multivariate rearrangement theorem.

For any coupling and any positive call event of mass r, each coordinate
restriction is a submeasure of mass r. Its first moment is at most the
upper-r quantile first moment, including split threshold atoms. The
weighted sum therefore gives the claimed call inequality. Equal total
mass and first moment then give convex order. Continuous convex tests
follow directly by piecewise-linear approximation. If 'every convex real
function on the compact range' includes upward discontinuities at an
endpoint, these are harmless too: endpoint atoms are limits of scaled
calls, or their reflected versions, so the same comparison covers their
nonnegative endpoint jumps.

The density argument has the correct direction. A target density bounded
by a_i gives a quantile expansion at least 1/a_i, and the weighted sum
therefore has expansion at least sum lambda_i/a_i. The inverse image of
an interval has the corresponding length bound. Countable interval
coverings extend this to all Borel sets. Support gaps and quantile jumps
can only increase expansion, so neither strict positivity nor smoothness
is being assumed. Uniform interval examples realize equality.

For branch masses lambda_i m, rescaling alpha_i by 1/lambda_i produces
equal-mass marginals and density ceilings a_i=1/lambda_i. The coefficient
is consequently 1/sum lambda_i^2, as printed. For the equal two-branch
case this is the bound on the mass-2tau law; dividing by two recovers the
unit-density bound on the mass-tau midpoint law in the three-fiber note.
There is no missing factor of two.

The geometric support conclusion uses both actual hypotheses: anchored
compatibility gives membership in K_p, while exact support-height
equality forces membership in K_p(n). The continuous normal coordinate
is fixed there, so convex physical tests are exactly convex functions
of the one tangent coordinate. No center or actual fiber is replaced by
a formal measure.

The finite-normal scope is sound. The source explicitly does not
silently choose over a continuum of normals, change variable-dependent
barycentric weights into fixed weights, or infer halfspace domination
from convex order. Nor does it claim that all actual martingale rows
admit a parity-efficient decomposition into these fixed-weight groups.
Those are the remaining substantive inputs, not consequences of the
quantile calculation.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
